title: Spreading a stalk nonzerodivisor generator to a Cartier equation
statement: Let $B$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $I\subseteq B$ an ideal and $\mathfrak p$ a prime ideal. Suppose $IB_{\mathfrak p}=(t)$ where multiplication by $t$ on $B_{\mathfrak p}$ is injective [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. There exist $g\in B\setminus\mathfrak p$ and $a\in I$ such that $IB_g=(a/1)$ and multiplication by $a/1$ on $B_g$ is injective, where $B_g$ is localization at the powers of $g$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. More generally let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth] and $H\hookrightarrow X$ a closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion]. If the stalk [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] at every $x\in X$ of its ideal sheaf $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], as an ideal $\mathcal I_x\subseteq\mathcal O_{X,x}$, is generated by a nonzerodivisor, then $\mathcal I$ is an effective Cartier ideal [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. At a point outside $H$ the unit generator $1$ is permitted, and the empty closed subscheme is included. No reducedness, integrality or regularity of the ambient scheme is assumed.

source.place:
Tag 0AG8 (lemma-effective-Cartier-in-points), with the nonzerodivisor spreading argument via the finitely generated annihilator. Proof handoff retained verbatim under the released re-split order; these are the old parent arguments to implement, not proof steps of this statement-only node. Original parent step 6: Here is the finite-denominator argument making these stalk equations effective Cartier equations on open neighborhoods; no global equation is being assumed. Fix $x$, choose an affine $\operatorname{Spec}B$ as in step 1, and let $J$ define $H$. Since $J_{\mathfrak p}$ has a nonzerodivisor generator, express that generator as $a/s$ with $a\in J$ and $s
otin\mathfrak p$. Then $a/1$ also generates $J_{\mathfrak p}$ and is a nonzerodivisor. Write a finite generating list $b_1,\ldots,b_m$ for $J$. Each membership $b_j/1\in(a/1)$ can be cleared by the fraction equality rule. Multiplying the finitely many denominators gives $u
otin\mathfrak p$ such that $J B_u=aB_u$. The ideal $\operatorname{Ann}_B(a)$ is also finitely generated. Each of its generators vanishes in $B_{\mathfrak p}$, so multiplication by another $v
otin\mathfrak p$ kills them all. Multiplication by $a$ is injective on $B_{uv}$: a fraction annihilated by $a$ has numerator, after multiplying by a power of $uv$, in $\operatorname{Ann}_B(a)$, and hence is zero there. Thus $J B_{uv}$ has nonzerodivisor generator $a$. These neighborhoods cover $X$, proving the effective Cartier ideal condition. This argument also covers a point outside $H$, where the generator can be $1$.
Cited statements: def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal.

proof.text: Work with any algebra S that localizes B at p, so the same argument applies both to Localization.AtPrime p and directly to an affine structure-sheaf stalk. The localized-ideal membership criterion writes t*s = a/1 for a in I and s outside p. The unit s/1 preserves the span and injectivity, so a/1 generates I S and multiplication by a/1 is injective.

proof.text: Choose a finite generating set F of I. For each b in F, membership of b/1 in (a/1) and IsLocalization.algebraMap_mem_map_algebraMap_iff give u_b outside p with u_b*b in (a). Independently choose a finite generating set T of ker(B -> S). Each k in T has v_k outside p with v_k*k = 0 by IsLocalization.map_eq_zero_iff. Put g = product(u_b)*product(v_k), which lies outside p. Span induction and divisibility by each factor show g*I is contained in (a) and g*ker(B -> S) = 0. If a*z=0, injectivity at p implies z lies in that kernel; hence g*z=0.

proof.text: The proved source-library Ideal.isRegularPrincipal_map_away applies to g, I, a and these two clearing properties: I in any localization away from g is regular principal. In the canonical Localization.Away g, explicitly divide the equation g*b = d*a by the unit g/1 to identify the ideal with span(a/1). The proved mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_span_singleton_eq transfers regularity to this prescribed generator, and cancellation on a difference yields the required injectivity. Both source lemmas are imported through the effective-Cartier-ideal module; neither assumes a domain.

proof.text: For each x, choose the affine U, t and ideal-extension equality supplied by the hypothesis. The affine section ring B is Noetherian by IsLocallyNoetherian.component_noetherian. The affine ring germ is a localization at the prime of x by IsAffineOpen.isLocalization_stalk. Apply the generic finite-clearing argument of steps 1--2 directly to this algebra and the given t; this yields g outside that prime, a in the affine ideal, and the two clearing properties.

proof.text: Since the germ of g is a unit, Scheme.mem_basicOpen shows x belongs to D(g). This is affine and its section ring is a localization away from g by IsAffineOpen.isLocalization_basicOpen. IdealSheafData.map_ideal identifies its ideal with the extension of the ideal on U. Apply the proved Ideal.isRegularPrincipal_map_away to this section ring and the clearing properties from step 4. Thus every x has an affine neighbourhood with regular-principal ideal, exactly IdealSheafData.IsInvertible. Units, empty closed subschemes and empty ambient schemes are included without any extra case assumption.
